title: Heat Transfer 1 — One-Dimensional Heat Flux Through a Plane Wall
statement:
A flat wall made of stainless steel separates two regions held at different temperatures. Assume steady-state, one-dimensional conduction with constant thermal conductivity and no heat generation.

Given:
- Thermal conductivity, k = 16.0 W/m·K
- Wall thickness, L = 0.025 m
- Hot-side surface temperature, T_hot = 150 °C
- Cold-side surface temperature, T_cold = 90 °C

Use Fourier’s law for one-dimensional conduction to determine the heat flux through the wall. Take the positive x-direction from the hot side toward the cold side.

parts.prompt: Calculate the temperature gradient dT/dx across the wall.
Calculate the one-dimensional heat flux q'' through the wall.

common_mistakes: Using the wall thickness in centimeters instead of meters
Dropping the negative sign in Fourier’s law without considering direction
Using T_hot - T_cold when the defined x-direction is from hot to cold and then applying the sign incorrectly
hints: Write the temperature gradient first, then apply Fourier’s law.
Check the sign convention based on the positive x-direction.
Heat should flow from the hotter side to the colder side.
